attribution.note: Marcus explicitly endorses the point and states both the historical claim and forecast in his own words.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the historical component and firm forecast of many additional cases, without adding a deadline or requiring autonomous intent.

contract.note: Counting measured manipulation in real human experiments is an ordinary reading of the unrestricted claim. Substantial additional instances need not establish rising population incidence, though this interpretation determines resolution.

evidence.note: The prepublication research reports actual human behavioral effects from adversarial strategies, including exploitation of trust. It supports the historical component.

The 2025 preprint reports controlled increases in actual human engagement across five manipulative conditions and examines numerous conversations. It supports substantial additional manipulation; neither total enrollment nor every reply is a count of successful manipulation.

reviews.rationale: The historical experiments establish prepublication manipulation. The dated 2025 study establishes numerous subsequent human interactions with controlled behavioral effects, satisfying the contract's early-resolution rule on a fair plain reading. The evidence does not establish everyday population incidence or imply every participant was manipulated; neither is required.
